Wings and Woodlands: A Tribute to Native Birds and Forests

2026 Art Exhibit | Kaua‘i Society of Artists Gallery | Kukui Grove Center

The Kaua‘i Forest Bird Recovery Project and Birds Not Mosquitoes are partnering again with the Kaua‘i Endangered Seabird Recovery Project to celebrate Hawai’i’s native manu through art!

Exhibit Dates: Nov 7 – Nov 12, 2026
 Opening Reception: Nov 6, 2026

We invite artists of all ages and experience levels to submit 2D & 3D artwork inspired by Kaua‘i’s native birds and their habitats, including: Paintings, drawings, sculptures, photographs, and featherwork.

Artwork Submission Guidelines:

Mail/Drop off Locations:

  • By Mail:  KFBRP, PO Box 57 PO Box 57 (USPS mail) OR C/O Gay & Robinson Field Office, Building 800 (Courier) 1 Kaumakani Ave, Kaumakani, HI 96747
  • Hand-Delivery:
    • Primary Location:
       DOFAW Field Operations Baseyard
      4398 Pua Loke St. #D, Lihue, HI 96766
      Google Maps Pin

(Drop off instructions:  It’s a bit tricky to find- you’ll have to continue down our small street past the old water department building and the ag department, to a parking lot at the end of the street. Park there and call our office phone number at 808-555-0100, and someone can come out and meet you to show you where our office is.)

  • Alternative Drop-Off:
     KSA Gallery (Kukui Grove Center)
    November 4th: 1PM-6PM and November 5th: 1PM-6PM (Do not drop off at the gallery before

Northshore Drop-Off:

Please contact Thomas Daubert (someone@example.org) to coordinate drop off.

  • For Digital Art Work
    • Please send to someone@example.org by 10/30/2026

Display & Sales Options –  Artists may choose to:

  • Display only (must pick up artwork post-exhibit)
  • Donate a portion of sales (25%, 50%, or 75%)
  • Donate your artwork

All wall art must have hanging wire securely attached.

Selection & Display Criteria:

Our goal is to celebrate our native birds and display as many artists as possible. If space runs out, priority will be given to:

  • Artwork received by Oct 30, 2026
  • Art featuring Kaua‘i’s native birds
  • Pieces showcasing Hawaiian native birds
  • Ensuring each artist has at least one piece displayed
  • Higher percentage of sales donated

Note: We have not run out of space in previous exhibits.

Let your creativity take flight! Capture the vibrant colors, unique features, and beauty of Hawai‘i’s forest birds.

Mahalo to all the artists helping to showcase and protect these incredible manu!

Find all details HERE.

Saturday, May 2 at 7:00 AM at Vidinha Stadium!

This event is a great way to support our efforts to protect Kauaʻi’s endangered forest birds—and enjoy a fun morning walk through Līhu‘e with friends,’ohana and fellow conservation supporters.

Here’s how you can help:
1⃣ Donate to support our Charity Walk team.
2⃣ Register to walk with us! The $50 registration includes a t-shirt and breakfast.
3⃣ If you’re walking, invite friends and ‘ohana to support your efforts through the event’s online tools.

The best part? Every dollar raised will be matched—dollar for dollar—by the event’s proceeds!

It’s a powerful way to make twice the impact for Kauaʻi’s native species.

REGISTER OR DONATE HERE.

Mahalo for standing with us and helping to protect the birds that make our island home so special.

]]> DINE FOR A CAUSE – ALL FEBRUARY LONG https://kauaiforestbirds.org/dine-for-a-cause-all-february-long/ Wed, 04 Feb 2026 01:31:43 +0000 https://kauaiforestbirds.org/?p=3856
We’re excited to share that we have been selected as the nonprofit recipient for proceeds from Table 53 at RumFire Poipu!
By dining at Table 53, you’re directly supporting efforts to protect Kauaʻi’s native forest birds and their habitats. It’s an easy (and delicious!) way to give back.
Call RumFire (808-742-4RUM) to make your reservation and request Table 53, and dine knowing your meal is making a difference.
Mahalo for supporting bird conservation on Kauaʻi!
